# openmetadata_ml_model_service (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata ML model service. ML model services are the connection containers for ML models.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_ml_model_service" "churn_tracking" {
  name         = "churn-tracking"
  service_type = "Mlflow"
  display_name = "Churn model tracking"
  description  = "ML model service backing the churn models."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) ML model service name. Changing it replaces the service, because the name is also its fully qualified name.
- `service_type` (String) OpenMetadata service type such as Mlflow, Sklearn, SageMaker, VertexAI, CustomMlModel. The server fixes it at creation, so changing it replaces the service.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Markdown description of the ML model service.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.

### Read-Only

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name. For an ML model service this equals name.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_ml_model_service.churn_tracking 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name, which for an ML model service is its name.
terraform import openmetadata_ml_model_service.churn_tracking churn-tracking
```
